strongest_argument: Every input is a line in So-Young's own quarterly press release, and the headline number is an artefact of a definition change the company itself disclosed. The Q2'25 table is headed 'Phase (The length of time since establishment)' - legal registration - while from Q3'25 it reads 'commencement of actual operations', adds an Average Center Age column, re-dates relocated or merged centres to the predecessor's start (pushing established higher-revenue units up into Maturity), excludes temporarily-closed periods (pushing renovation-disrupted units down into Growth) and drops converted centres entirely. The whole '26% over four quarters' is the single non-comparable step at that break: 6.403 to 4.818 is -24.7%, and the three like-for-like quarters that follow are 4.818, 4.682, 4.760 - flat, with the last UP sequentially, while the cohort's average age rose 6.5 to 7.1 to 8.0 months and membership grew 15 to 19 to 23. The claim's central mechanism, that each new vintage ramps to a permanently lower plateau, is refuted by the same published table: the Maturity cohort, where those vintages land, went 7.271 to 8.384 to 7.500 (the Chinese New Year trough), up 3% versus Q3'25 even while absorbing six graduating vintages and expanding from 14 to 20 centres. The forward leg is weaker still: that the RMB307-317m guide 'implies per-centre revenue falls again' is arithmetic on a figure management published on 2026-05-22, where management stated it expects per-centre revenue to keep climbing. The industry corroboration is the most published part of all - Bloomberg ran the Chinese aesthetics price-war story on 2025-09-21 naming So-Young itself as the price-cutter.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Publishes the exact cohort table the claim rests on - Growth 23 centres, avg age 8.0 months, RMB4.760m per centre - plus the Phase footnote on actual-operations dating and the exclusions, and the Q2 guide.

The quarter of the alleged break: Growth 15 centres, avg age 6.5 months, RMB4.818m, with the new full Phase footnote quoted verbatim - the definitional change is disclosed in the release itself, not hidden.

The baseline quarter's table is headed 'length of time since establishment' with three columns, no Average Center Age and no footnote - confirming RMB6.403m is computed on a registration-date basis and is not comparable to what follows.
Q4'25: Growth 19 centres at RMB4.682m; Maturity 17 centres at RMB8.384m - the maturity cohort rising, contradicting the permanently-lower-plateau mechanism.
Bloomberg publishes the Chinese aesthetics price-deflation story on the wire and names So-Young as the instigator.
Published downgrade to Hold whose entire thesis is that revenue acceleration is bought with widening losses from footprint expansion - the economic implication the claim tries to introduce as new.

baseline_evidence: Options give no support either way: skew null, 200 contracts, ATM bid-ask 40% of mid, and the baseline itself flags priced_direction_available false. The tape argues against a fresh negative: spot -46.3% from the 52-week high means the de-rating on exactly this complex has already happened, and the stock is +30.4% over 20 days into the print. The cleanest datum is the 2026-05-22 reaction: roughly -12% on the day the Q1'26 cohort table, the RMB4.760m growth figure and the guide were all published together.
materiality: cannot tell, and arguably immaterial as stated. Like-for-like the move is -1.2% over three quarters (4.818 to 4.760) on a cohort that grew from 15 to 23 centres. The claimed -26% is not measurable against any consistent definition because the Q2'25 denominator uses registration dates and the later ones operating dates.
what_would_change_my_verdict: A like-for-like series showing growth-cohort revenue per centre falling materially with average centre age held constant, or evidence that Q2'26 aesthetic treatment revenue lands below the published RMB307m floor - the only version of this the print can resolve.
